preamble: Affrication of the palatal stop [c] to the postalveolar affricate [tʃ] adds a fricated release and moves the closure slightly forward. It is the usual second step in velar palatalization chains (k > c > tʃ), and it is observed directly where a palatal stop phoneme exists: Albanian q /c/ merges with ç /tʃ/ for many speakers, Macedonian ќ /c/ has merged with /tʃ/ in the urban Prilep subdialect, and Basque palatal tt, [c] in Goizueta, is pronounced as tx [tʃ] in Gipuzkoan and Biscayan.

examples.note: The merger of the palatal stops q, gj into the palatoalveolar affricates ç, xh is especially common in Northern Gheg and spreading in Tosk.
In the urban Prilep subdialect of the Prilep-Bitola dialect, ќ and ѓ have merged into /tʃ/ and /dʒ/; northern dialects have alveolo-palatal [tɕ dʑ] instead.
In Gipuzkoan and Biscayan the palatal tt of expressive palatalization is pronounced the same as the affricate tx [tʃ].

sources: Hualde, J. I., Lujanbio, O. & Zubiri, J. J. (2010). Goizueta Basque. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 40, 113–127. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100309990260
